$comment: Leg lifecycle: the states a leg moves through, the events that move it, and the intervals that fall due. This is to the internal registry what faults.json is to the public portal - the table the UI reads rather than hard-codes. The registry keys every leg on its MECHANICAL serial because that is the number permanent for the life of the frame; the electronics serial is a current binding, and swapping it is an event, not a new leg.

identity.note: Wear, intervals, warranty and the lease record accrue against the frame. Firmware, pairing and session assignment follow the electronics. A registry keyed on the electronics serial would reset a leg's history every time a ClearCore was swapped.

states.label: Built
states.description: The mechanical serial has been stamped and the frame exists. The leg has no operational identity yet and cannot be assigned.

states.label: Commissioned
states.description: A ClearCore has been bound, firmware loaded and both axes tested. The leg has both identities but has not been released to the fleet.

states.label: In pool
states.description: Healthy, charged and available to be assigned to a session or sent out as a replacement.

states.label: Deployed
states.description: Held by a facility. May or may not be claimed into a session right now; the session controller owns that, not the registry.

states.label: In transit
states.description: Moving between a facility and ERS, in either direction. A failed leg riding back with the driver who brought its replacement is in transit, not deployed.

states.label: On the line
states.description: Checked in and moving through the ERS reconditioning line. The stage field carries which station it is at.

states.label: In service
states.description: Diverted out of the line - either on a flag filed from the field or on failing inspection. Work is open against the frame.

states.label: Quarantined
states.description: Held out of the fleet pending a decision. Nothing assigns a quarantined leg, and nothing clears it automatically.

states.label: Retired
states.description: Permanently withdrawn. The record stays - a retired frame still has a lease and warranty history written against its number.

events.label: Electronics swapped
events.note: Rolls the operational identity over. History stays on the frame.

events.label: Dispatch requested
events.note: Filed from the field against the electronics serial. The leg cannot finish its session.

events.label: Flagged for ERS
events.note: Filed from the field against the mechanical serial. Read at inspection.

events.label: Service record closed
events.note: The only event that clears SES-30. A controller swap does not.

intervals.note: Whichever comes first, accrued against the mechanical serial and reset only by a closed service record. Reaching one is a flag, not a dispatch - a leg at its interval is not a leg in trouble.

reconciliation.note: A leg a facility believes it holds but which the registry has not heard from in this long is reported, not searched for. The registry exists so a moved leg resolves as bookkeeping rather than a loss.

viewer.label: Read only
viewer.note: Can look a leg up and read its history.

operator.label: Operator
operator.note: Can enter legs, record events and move state.
